% RETURN, REBASED · EOD 2026-11-11
DEFENSIVES LEADCyclicals -6.8% vs defensives on the month
Rotation ReadCitrini · claude

Defensive sectors are leading a violent rotation, and the cyclical unwind is the only thing that matters today. XLP leads at 11.55% in the last month and XLV is right behind at 10.66%, while XLK has collapsed -19.61% and XLI is down -5.31% with XLC off -6.55%. Year to date the picture inverts. XLE still holds 35.01% and XLV 18.91%, but XLK sits on 12.53% after giving back a fifth of its value in four weeks. You are watching a violent handoff from momentum leadership into defensives, and the magnitude says this is a de-risking event, not a gentle rebalance.

The theme data confirms the same story with more edge. Quantum is down 38.5% in a month, AI infra -35.0%, semis -34.9% and cyber -22.4%. These are the highest-beta growth baskets taking the worst damage. The leaders are biotech at 9.8% and GLP-1 at 7.6%, both health care complex plays. Defense is barely positive at 1.7% and banks flat at 0.1%. The only theme holding a strong YTD gain that is still bleeding is energy, down 3.1% on the month despite 43.4% year to date. That is profit taking in the last crowded winner standing.

The stretched ratios flag the same tension from a different angle. XLI/XLP sits at a z-score of -3.25, in the bottom 0% of its yearly range by range rank terms, meaning the ratio is at its most depressed level of the year. XLV/SPY is at +2.96, in the top 100% of its range. The market has already priced a full defensive rotation and then some. The second-order implication is uncomfortable. When a defensive ratio reaches these extremes, you are closer to a mean-reversion bounce than to continuation. Size your defensive overweight smaller than the momentum suggests and keep dry powder for the cyclical snap-back that follows an overshoot this severe.

Defensives leading hard while the cyclical and growth ratios hit their most compressed levels of the year.

BULL

The rotation into XLP, XLV and biotech is a healthy de-risking that resets crowded growth positioning. Once the selling in semis and AI infra exhausts, capital has somewhere to rotate back to.

BEAR

XLK down -19.61% and quantum down 38.5% on the month is disorderly unwinding, not rotation. If defensives keep absorbing flows, the growth complex has no floor until the ratio extremes revert.

TELL

Watch XLI/XLP at a z-score of -3.25. A bounce back toward its mean would confirm the cycle has bottomed and the defensive bid is fading.

⚠ Cyclical sectors are getting crushed: XLI down **-5.31%** and XLE down **-3.33%** on the month. vs XLI/XLP at a z-score of **-3.25** in the bottom **0%** of its yearly range signals the cyclical-to-defensive ratio has already overshot to the downside.: The sector returns confirm the rotation is real but the stretched ratio says it has gone too far. Trust the ratio for timing: cyclicals are near a mean-reversion bounce even though the monthly damage is severe.
⚠ Biotech leads themes at **9.8%** and XLV leads sectors, indicating a broad defensive bid. vs XLV/SPY at **+2.96** in the top **100%** of its range means health care relative strength is at an extreme.: Health care is both the leader and the most stretched ratio. Trust the trend for now but the extreme reading says the incremental upside from here is thin; the crowded positioning is the risk.

The extremes split cleanly into reversion candidates and confirmed trends. GDXJ/GDX at -3.34 and XLI/XLP at -3.25 are the most compressed readings in the data, both in the bottom 0% of their yearly range, and both look stretched enough to snap back.

XME/XLB at -3.11 is another cyclical-to-broad-materials ratio at its yearly low, while IWF/IWD at -2.63 and IWO/IWN at -2.48 show small caps and growth blowing off relative to value and large caps. The confirmed trend sits on the other side.

XLV/SPY at +2.96 and QUAL/SPY at +2.46 are in the top 100% of their ranges, and those are trend readings, not reversion signals. Health care and quality are working because the market wants safety and balance sheet strength.

You trust the XLV/SPY and QUAL/SPY extremes as directionally real and treat the cyclical ratios as oversold bounces waiting to happen.
